# Historical vault compatibility fixtures (S01 / #32)

All entries, passwords and secrets here are synthetic, public test data. Never
use them for accounts. `manifest.json` records each file's SHA-256, exact source
commit, password and expected decrypted model. Binary files are immutable test
inputs, not generated by the current writer during tests.

| Source release | Format | KDF | Current support |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v0.5.0 / 9cc8f643137df12b87484c9bb00caa4e40d16fd4 | salt + nonce + ciphertext + tag (no header) | Argon2id v19, t=3, m=65536 KiB, p=2, 32-byte key | Unsupported |
| v0.7.3 / 55708399428820f2f01182d561ff0cf570e53d48 | D2FA v1 | Argon2id v19, t=4, m=131072 KiB, p=2, 32-byte key | Supported with non-empty password |
| v0.8.3 / cd8c3aeff9f192edf650a8b0f007a62da75224a2 | D2FA v1 | Same as v0.7.3 | Supported with non-empty password |
| v0.8.3 (empty-password API variant) | D2FA v1 | Same as v0.7.3 | Unsupported since v0.9.0 |

All use UTF-8 password bytes, a 16-byte salt, AES-256-GCM with a 12-byte
nonce, a 16-byte tag and no AAD. D2FA v1 adds `D2FA` + `0x01` before the
salt (offsets: salt 5, nonce 21, ciphertext 33). Each payload has version 1
and three entries covering all hash algorithms, 6/7/8 digits and 30/45/60-second
periods. The third entry deliberately has a null account name: public loading
preserves it, with no automatic issuer-to-name migration. Unicode labels and
a Unicode non-empty password also pin UTF-8 behavior.

Produced on Windows with Python 3.13.11, argon2-cffi 25.1.0, cryptography 46.0.3
and Pydantic 2.12.5 using the historical `Vault.save()` and
historical models/crypto modules, extracted directly from the pinned Git commits.
Only package initializers are replaced with empty files to avoid unrelated CLI
imports. No production modules are modified. To intentionally regenerate from
the repository root (requires historical Git objects and dev dependencies):

```powershell
.venv/Scripts/python.exe tests/fixtures/vaults/generate.py --output ./vault-fixtures-new
```

The output directory must not exist and its parent must exist. The generator
stages all binaries and the manifest in a temporary sibling directory, then
publishes the complete snapshot with a single directory rename. Failure or
interruption before publication leaves existing fixtures untouched. It refuses
to overwrite any existing directory, including the committed fixture directory.
Historical writers receive public synthetic credentials over stdin; no generated
Python script stores passwords. Passwords in the manifest are intentionally
public test data, not application or user credentials.

Fresh salts/nonces mean regeneration changes hashes. Review a new snapshot's
binaries and manifest together before replacing the committed test data in Git.
The generator is a maintenance tool;
tests read committed fixtures without invoking Git or historical code.

Unsupported files must fail explicitly; they are not evidence of migration
support. The current loader cannot recover pre-header files. A historical
empty-password API vault must be opened and re-saved with a non-empty password
using the previous release before upgrading (see the root README). No fallback
or recovery implementation is added by S01.

Normal saves replace only the selected file. An explicit CLI `backup` creates a
separately encrypted snapshot; it need not be byte-identical to the source.
Tests recover its entries and check that later saves leave that snapshot intact.
Fixtures cover these identified releases, not every historical release or OS.
